payload.title: TI P4-09: apply the copy, convert bodies to Markus, fidelity check against the baseline
payload.description:
## Goal
The standard staging site (drafts rendered as if published, editors and admins only) on the new app, and a full dogfood pass of the backend CMS UX: create a draft, preview it on staging, publish it, see it on production. Mirrors Pilobol.us P3-07 (PPY-d0c5ad).

## Context (FACT)
- Template (lib/amplify-app-shell.ts): with cms.staging not false it creates branch staging (stage BETA) with its own build spec, env PAPYRUS_CONTENT_SOURCE=drafts, SITE_ENV=staging and NEXT_PUBLIC_PAPYRUS_STAGING_URL; for a Pretext site staging is a second Next build of the same app reading drafts through the production backend, behind the Cognito gate (middleware). A staging domain is created only when a staging host resolves; default derivation would be staging.anth.us (collision): set cms.stagingDomainName explicitly (see P4-05); until P4-11 staging runs on https://staging.<newAppId>.amplifyapp.com.
- Console connect of the app deletes branches: connect the staging branch in the console after the first connect (docs/site-hosting.md).
- Pretext pages use revalidate = 3600 (ISR). Without wiring, a publish becomes visible on production after up to one hour. On-demand revalidation exists (POST /api/revalidate with header x-papyrus-revalidate-secret; backend option revalidateBaseUrl and secret PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET read by the publish Lambda), but the template has no secret-safe way to set PAPYRUS_REVALIDATE_SECRET on the frontend branches: the secret cannot go in the public site.json, and a console-entered branch variable is wiped by the next stack update. The old site stored it as a plain branch variable (its value was visible in get-app output: do not reuse it). Open question Q7.
- Old pool has 1 admin, 2 editors; new pool users arrive through P4-07.

## Exact steps
1. site.json: cms.staging true, cms.stagingDomainName per Q8 (or none until P4-11); Ryan yes to the stack update; push git branch staging from main; connect the branch in the console; re-apply env vars by stack update if lost.
2. Probes (adapt scripts/staging-auth-test.mjs from the Pilobol.us work): anonymous GET on staging redirects to sign-in without a loop; an editor sees a draft with the STAGING banner and the same URL is 404 on production; a non-editor is refused; robots Disallow and noindex on staging; main has no staging-only variables (names).
3. Dogfood script with Ryan: in /newsroom create a draft article, edit it with the article editor, save, see it on staging, publish, see it on production (measure the delay), unpublish, see it removed; record friction points as Kanbus bugs under PPY-655994 or this phase.
4. Implement the Q7 answer: either accept hourly ISR and document it, or add the smallest secret-safe path (build spec reads the secret from SSM with the service role into .env.production) as a Papyrus change.

## Acceptance checks
- All probes pass and are recorded; staging shows the draft, production does not.
- Publish to visible-on-production delay measured and recorded; matches the Q7 decision.
- Friction list filed.

## Rollback
Set cms.staging false and redeploy; delete the staging branch.

## Risks
Build time 10 to 15 minutes per branch. Staging reads the production backend (accepted by Ryan: no second backend).

## Needs Ryan
Yes: stack update, console branch connect, sign-in as editor and non-editor, answers Q7 and Q8, and the dogfood session itself.

## Common rules (Phase 4 Threat Intelligence)
- Plan and facts: the assessment comment on the Phase 4 ticket (PPY-332889). Pattern: docs/migrations/pilobol-us.md and docs/standard-site.md 3.2 on origin/develop.
- Ryan: Threat Intelligence is PRE-PRODUCTION; goal is to dogfood the new backend CMS UX before converting anth.us (production). Treat as a hard cutover with brief downtime accepted unless Ryan says otherwise (open question Q1). The OLD app d3on1y5vlrxmam and its backend stay untouched and serving until the retire ticket.
- Read AGENTS.local.md first. AWS_PROFILE=legacy, us-east-1 (SSO is Ryan's). Never print env var or secret VALUES (names only). Never run ampx pipeline-deploy locally. Creating, changing or deleting AWS resources needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step; deleting data or stacks is done by Ryan or on his explicit yes. Read-only AWS calls are fine.
- NEVER use /Users/home/Projects/Pilobol.us as a build dir. TI repo work: fresh clone under /Users/home/Projects/ (delete afterwards), feature branch + PR, never push to its main. Papyrus repo: worktree of origin/develop under /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus-worktrees/, branch feature/PPY-<id>-<slug>, PR into develop, never merge to main, never git stash, trailer Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>, PR body ends with the Claude Code generated-with line. In /Users/home/Projects/Papyrus (the board checkout) only run kbs; never git add or commit there.
- Gherkin first for any Papyrus behavior change (AGENTS.md). Long clear names, no line-level comments.
- Update this ticket with branch, PR link and command output when done.
